claims.claim: Intl.DateTimeFormat('he-IL') renders the short date with dot separators (DD.MM.YYYY, e.g. 04.03.2026), not slashes; the long form is '4 במרץ 2026'. Re-run on Node v20.19.6 (ICU 78.1) on 2026-09-15.
claims.raw_snippet: The Intl.DateTimeFormat object enables language-sensitive date and time formatting.
claims.verified_via: runtime: node -e with Intl.DateTimeFormat('he-IL', {year:'numeric',month:'2-digit',day:'2-digit'}) returned 04.03.2026 for 2026-03-04

claims.claim: CLDR Hebrew cardinal plural rules: one is 'i = 1 and v = 0 or i = 0 and v != 0' (so decimals below 1 such as 0.5 select one), two is 'i = 2 and v = 0', other is everything else including 0, 3+, 100, 1.5 and 2.5. The many category was removed in CLDR 42 (2022).
claims.raw_snippet: <pluralRule count="one">i = 1 and v = 0 or i = 0 and v != 0 @integer 1 @decimal 0.0~0.9, 0.00~0.05</pluralRule>

claims.claim: Released vue-i18n (npm latest 11.4.10) picks plural cases by position: pluralDefault returns Math.min(choice, 2) for three cases (zero | one | other), so Hebrew needs a custom rule; {count} and {n} are predefined named arguments.
claims.raw_snippet:
// zero (0) | singular (1) | plural (2)
  return Math.min(choice, 2)

claims.claim: vue-i18n v11 custom pluralization is passed to createI18n as pluralRules (Composition API) or pluralizationRules (legacy Options API), with a rule function receiving (choice, choicesLength, orgRule).
claims.raw_snippet: 2. `pluralRules` (for Composition API)

claims.claim: In vue-i18n v11, createI18n runs in legacy mode unless legacy: false is passed (the legacy feature flag defaults to true), and legacy mode reads only pluralizationRules, so pluralRules requires legacy: false.
claims.raw_snippet:
: __FEATURE_LEGACY_API__ && isBoolean(options.legacy)
      ? options.legacy
      : __FEATURE_LEGACY_API__

claims.claim: vue-i18n v11 legacy option conversion reads options.pluralizationRules and maps it to the composer pluralRules.
claims.raw_snippet: const pluralizationRules = options.pluralizationRules

claims.claim: Automatic pluralization with Intl.PluralRules is a breaking (feat!) change on the vue-i18n main branch, not present in the 11.x runtime.
claims.raw_snippet: feat!: Support automatic pluralization with `Intl.PluralRules`

claims.claim: i18next selects plural key suffixes (_one, _two, _other) via Intl.PluralRules; React Native's Hermes does not implement Intl.PluralRules, and since i18next v24 there is no fallback, so without a polyfill (intl-pluralrules) only English-style _one/_other resolve.
claims.raw_snippet: Since i18next v24 there is no fallback: without Intl only English-style `_one`/`_other` forms resolve.

claims.claim: In next-intl setup for Next.js 16, the middleware file is proxy.ts; it was called middleware.ts up until Next.js 16. The matcher is '/((?!api|trpc|_next|_vercel|.*\\..*).*)'.
claims.raw_snippet: **Note:** `proxy.ts` was called `middleware.ts` up until Next.js 16.

claims.claim: dir="auto" should be used for data with unknown directionality such as user input; the browser uses the first strongly directional character, so text that starts with an English name gets a left-to-right base direction.
claims.raw_snippet: The `auto` value should be used for data with an unknown directionality, like data coming from user input or external data.
